news.headline: NeurAxis Announces Medical Coverage Policy Milestone, Expanding Access to Over 18 Million Additional Covered Lives
news.summary: NeurAxis secured new medical policy coverage from a major national health insurer for PENFS across multiple states, adding roughly 18 million covered lives and pushing its total national coverage footprint above 120 million lives. Shares moved higher on the news as investors continue to reward IB-Stim reimbursement progress.

news.headline: NeurAxis to Participate in the Lytham Partners Fall 2026 Investor Conference
news.summary: NeurAxis said it will host a webcast presentation and one-on-one investor meetings at the virtual Lytham Partners Fall 2026 Investor Conference on September 29-30, 2026. The presentation is scheduled for 11:45 a.m. ET on September 29.

news.headline: NeurAxis Presents at IAccess Alpha Virtual Best Ideas Fall Investment Conference, Citing Payer Wins Driving Growth
news.summary: Management presented NeurAxis's growth case to investors, emphasizing that its clinical evidence base, expanding payer coverage, and the new Category I CPT code (effective January 2026) are setting up an accelerating growth phase for IB-Stim in pediatric gut-brain disorders.

news.headline: NeurAxis Grants RSUs to Executives and Directors Following One-for-One Stock Option Exchange
news.summary: Following a shareholder-approved stock option exchange effective July 24, 2026, NeurAxis's CEO, CFO and other executives converted roughly 1.3 million legacy options into RSUs, and the compensation committee granted additional multi-year vesting RSUs to management and one-time equity awards to independent directors.

news.headline: NeurAxis Reports Record Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Driven by 116% Year-Over-Year Revenue Growth
news.summary: NeurAxis posted Q2 2026 revenue of $1.93 million, up 116% year-over-year, with unit deliveries up 60% and gross margin widening to 85.9%, though the $0.19 per-share loss missed consensus and the stock fell about 7% on the mixed print. Management called it the strongest quarter in company history, citing CPT Category I coding and payer coverage gains as growth drivers.

news.headline: NeurAxis Expands Payer Coverage with New Medical Policies
news.summary: NeurAxis announced four new medical policies covering PENFS/IB-Stim, including additional Mid-Atlantic regional coverage that expands access to more than 500,000 additional lives. The company said payer adoption continues to build on the January 2026 Category I CPT code.

catalysts.label: Lytham Partners Fall 2026 Investor Conference
catalysts.detail: NeurAxis will webcast a company presentation (Sept 29, 11:45 a.m. ET) and hold one-on-one investor meetings; potential venue for updated commercial/reimbursement metrics.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings and business update call
catalysts.detail: Based on the prior reporting cadence (Q1 in May, Q2 on Aug 11), NeurAxis's next quarterly results should land in November 2026, with focus on revenue growth trajectory, VA Federal Supply Schedule ramp, and further payer coverage wins. Exact date not yet announced.

catalysts.label: Additional payer medical-policy coverage decisions
catalysts.detail: NeurAxis has been announcing incremental insurer medical-policy coverage wins roughly monthly through 2026 (Mid-Atlantic in August, ~18M lives in September); further coverage announcements are a recurring near-term catalyst as the January 2026 Category I CPT code continues to be adopted by payers.

catalysts.label: Adult IBS/functional abdominal pain RCT topline data (Cleveland Clinic & Stanford)
catalysts.detail: A randomized, double-blind adult trial is underway at Cleveland Clinic and Stanford; positive data could open a much larger adult IBS/FAP market (management-cited ~$14B SAM) beyond the current pediatric label.

pulse: NeurAxis shares (~$6, market cap roughly $75M) have pulled back from their post-Q2 high after an EPS miss overshadowed 116% year-over-year revenue growth, but the reimbursement story keeps strengthening, with national payer coverage now exceeding 120 million lives following the new Category I CPT code that took effect in January 2026. The near-term narrative is being driven by steady incremental payer wins and investor-conference visibility (IAccess Alpha in mid-September, Lytham Partners at month-end) rather than a single binary catalyst, while the bigger longer-term optionality sits in ongoing adult-indication trials at Cleveland Clinic, Stanford and Emory that could expand IB-Stim beyond its current pediatric FDA clearance.
